The e2e soak catches exactly the failures unit tests structurally cannot: replay-timing races (cg6.1's tier jump), cross-leaf dedup windows (cg6.3), and the daemon-restart/mail-path interactions that only surface under sustained real cadence. Deterministic is the key qualifier — a scripted, repeatable soak (fixed seed, fixed interval, recorded event log) converts "flaky" from a shrug into a regression artifact: any diff in the deterministic trace across runs is a bug by construction. Without it, the durable-loop epic ships on trust; with it, we get the replay-determinism claim proven at the cadence where crashes actually happen.
